messages:
Anya: FYI — during today's maintenance we saw a ~2m controlplane connector outage to a subset of customer VPCs. Affected Dedicated tenants saw degraded API availability and we slipped a bit on our latency SLA. Opening this thread to capture short/medium/long term mitigations.

Michael: Timeline?

Anya: 12:15 UTC: ENI rotation started for the connector host in us-west-2 -> route flap -> connector lost its NAT path and restarted its agent. Controlplane mTLS reconnect took ~2m for some tenants. No data corruption, but requests failed with 502 during that window.

devops-bot: Incident INC-2026-234 created and linked to this thread.

Sam: Root cause summary?

Anya: Two things combined: (1) ENI swap + route propagation race, (2) connector's TLS handshake is single-threaded and waits on cert/key fetch, so re-establish took longer than expected.

Leila: Tradeoff space: fast reconnect vs cost/complexity. Options: (A) keep a lightweight standby relay in each AZ (incurs steady cost), (B) make connector handshake parallel + prefetch certs (engineering effort), (C) allow scoped public-relay fallback for non-Dedicated customers (policy/privacy tradeoffs).

Jordan: Option C is easiest to ship quickly but unacceptable for Private/Dedicated by contract. Could be opt-in for lower tiers though.

Kevin: For Dedicated customers we need SLA-safe solutions. Maybe per-customer policy: disallow public fallback unless explicitly agreed.

Sam: Practical short-term mitigation we can implement this week: shorten connector backoff and run a prewarm peering step ahead of planned ENI rotations. Also add a healthprobe that keeps NAT mappings alive during swap. Example probe command: `curl -sS https://controlplane.internal/health || true` run every 10s.

Leila: Agreed. Also add a brief TTL on controlplane route entries to avoid stale routes surviving too long after ENI swap. And add a small jitter to propagation to avoid synchronized flaps.

Anya: Proposal (staged):
- Short term (1 week): aggressive reconnect/backoff changes + healthprobe + canary the change for 5% of hosts.
- Mid term (1–2 months): implement prefetch/parallel TLS handshake and remove single-threaded blocking in the connector.
- Long term (3+ months): RFC for optional AZ-local standby relay and a secure, auditable public-fallback mode for non-Dedicated customers.

Jordan: Rollout plan details?

Anya: 1) Push the backoff + probe change to canary (5% hosts) tomorrow. 2) Monitor TTR-CP and error rates for 48h. 3) If stable, widen to 25% then 100% over the following week. 4) Kick off connector refactor RFC after canary validates.

Kevin: Add metrics now: time-to-restore-controlplane (TTR-CP), percent-fallback-routed, and connector-reconnect-latency. Console dashboards + alert when TTR-CP > 30s for Dedicated tenants.

Sam: I'll own the short-term PR and the healthprobe.

devops-bot: INC-2026-234 assigned to Sam, Leila.

Michael: +1. Also update the on-call playbook with the new temporary mitigation steps (prewarm peering, probe command) so responders can run them during rotation incidents.

Leila: I'll add the playbook snippet and the route-ttl change to the infra runbook.

Anya: I'll draft the RFC for the connector TLS refactor (parallel auth + token prefetch) and share in #architecture next week. Also will make a public-fallback opt-in policy doc for non-Dedicated customers.

Jordan: One more: we should simulate ENI rotation in a chaos run to measure TTR-CP before rolling wide. Recommend a small chaos test in staging after canary.

Anya: Good call — add chaos test to the canary checklist.

Kevin: Thanks all. Let's not let onboarding rotations bite us again :slightly_smiling_face:
